facts.content: Denies limb weakness and reports normal gait.
Patient has a history of kidney stones.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
There is a family history of hypothyroidism.
Acute unilateral headache with visual phenomena and nausea/vomiting is clinically consistent with migraine; first episode with no focal neurological symptoms by history.
facts.source_text: Acute unilateral HA with visual phenomena and N/V—clinically c/w migraine (first episode). No focal neuro sx by history.

facts.content: Patient to trial symptomatic treatment with ibuprofen and antiemetic available over the counter per pharmacy recommendation; advised to drink sugary carbonated beverage like cola.
facts.source_text: Trial symptomatic tx: ibuprofen + antiemetic (OTC per pharmacy); drink sugary carbonated beverage (e.g., cola)

facts.content: Arrange in-person visit today for a full neurological examination.

facts.content: Consider escalating to migraine-specific therapy if there is no response after assessment.
facts.source_text: If no response, consider stepping up to migraine-specific therapy after assessment

facts.content: Seek urgent care if worsening, new neurological symptoms, intractable vomiting, or severe escalation occur; call to cancel if markedly improved before the appointment.
